title: How to Make Good Habits Inevitable and Bad Habits Impossible
coreMove: Preload the environment so the good action is ready and the bad action is blocked.
sourcePressure: Good habits become far more likely when the environment keeps them available and ready, while bad habits weaken when stronger barriers make them hard to perform.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating commitment devices as perfect control instead of stronger default design.

hook: starting with a definition of commitment device
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a sleep clinic patient locking the router timer before bedtime
exampleSpecs.audience: a patient whose late streaming destroys CPAP compliance
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a barrier makes the bad habit harder before fatigue arrives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the router shuts off at 10:15 and the bedroom charger is already across the room
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a router timer glowing beside a CPAP case

exampleSpecs.domain: a marine rescue team pre-rigging throw bags before storm season
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer crew that loses minutes under pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether setup makes the right action inevitable when alarms sound
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the bag clips are already color-coded to boat seats, so no one chooses under stress
exampleSpecs.firstImage: orange throw bags clipped under a rescue boat bench

exampleSpecs.domain: a cafe owner putting pastry orders behind a pre-commitment cutoff
exampleSpecs.audience: a customer trying to stop impulse buying before dawn shifts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether removing day-of ordering changes the default
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she must place tomorrow order by 6 p.m.; at 6 a.m. the display is no longer a live choice
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an order cutoff card taped beside a pastry case

exampleSpecs.domain: a violin teacher auto-booking practice rooms for students after recital signups
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher making practice available without extra decisions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: attendance rises because each student receives a booked room code before the week begins
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a practice-room code slip tucked into a violin case

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal fleet manager installing fuel-card locks for idle-heavy trucks
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a structural barrier beats another reminder memo
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: drivers predict they will work around the lock, then the engine-off refuel sequence becomes the easiest route
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a fuel card locked in a dashboard sleeve

exampleSpecs.domain: a home dialysis patient setting supply cassettes in weekday bins every Sunday
exampleSpecs.audience: a patient whose evening fatigue causes skipped setup
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether ready supplies make the good action the obvious next move
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: on Wednesday night she opens the marked bin and begins without hunting through boxes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: weekday supply bins lined under a treatment chair

skillTargets: use commitment devices and availability design
preload good actions before choice moments
make unwanted actions harder without pretending choice disappears

tryThisNowSpec: Set up one future good action so it is ready before the moment of choice, then add one barrier to the tempting alternative.
